name: Citizenship by Marriage to a Honduran Citizen

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 24 lists persons married to native-born (by-birth) Hondurans as a distinct naturalization category, separate from the general residence-based tracks. The official application (published on sgjd.gob.hn) uses gender-neutral language throughout ('solicitante' / 'conyuge hondureno') -- no father/husband-only or mother/wife-only asymmetry found. Documentary requirements: authenticated passport copy, recent photograph, applicant's birth certificate, marriage certificate issued within the prior 30 days (legalized if the marriage occurred abroad), spouse's and children's birth certificates, foreign-registry certificate, migration movement certification, medical certificate, police/court clearance, and tax-solvency certificates. Fees are tiered by the applicant's own nationality: USD 200 for Central Americans, USD 300 for Ibero-Americans, USD 400 for other nationalities. Applicants must show 'patrimonio, profesion, oficio, actividad o industria licitos' (lawful means of self-support) or documented economic dependence on the spouse.
requirements.fix_path: Marry a Honduran-by-birth citizen, assemble the required documentation, pay the tiered fee, and apply through Honduras's digital procedures portal (SGJD).

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate (issued within 30 days, legalized if foreign)

sources.title: Sistema de Gestion de Justicia y Democracia (SGJD, Honduran government digital-procedures portal) -- official checklist and fees for naturalization based on marriage to a Honduran citizen
Georgetown University Political Database of the Americas -- hosted text of Honduras's 1982 Constitution, Article 24 (naturalization categories including marriage to a native-born Honduran)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Honduras). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- the hard requirement is sourced directly to sgjd.gob.hn, a Honduran government digital-procedures domain hosting the actual official application checklist, tier 1. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: gender-neutral in both the constitutional category and the official application's own wording -- no asymmetry found, unlike several other marriage-citizenship routes in this dataset (Syria, Guatemala, Zimbabwe). NOTABLE GAP, EXPLICITLY DISCLOSED: neither source reviewed states a minimum length of marriage or residence before this route can be used -- unlike most other countries' marriage-citizenship files in this dataset, no months-married threshold could be confirmed, so fix_time_months and citizenship_after_months are left null rather than assumed. dual_citizenship_allowed left null for this specific route since neither source addressed whether the treaty-dependent dual-nationality rule (Article 24, see hn_citizenship_naturalisation.json) applies the same way here.
